entities.name: P2RY2
observations: P2Y2 nucleotide receptor loss of function impairs collateral artery maturation and perfusion recovery after murine femoral artery ligation.
P2RY2-null mice show reduced early macrophage recruitment and vascular-cell proliferation, with increased late angiogenesis interpreted as compensation for persistent ischemia.

entities.name: Hind-limb ischemia
observations: In a murine femoral artery ligation model, P2RY2 deficiency causes persistent ischemia, tissue loss, and impaired recovery of limb perfusion.

entities.name: PMID:25088742 P2Y2 arteriogenesis
observations: Study compared wild-type and P2RY2-null mice after femoral artery ligation using serial laser-Doppler perfusion, Microfil collateral casting, and tissue immunohistology.

P2RY2-null mice achieved approximately 40% of wild-type perfusion recovery by day 28; collateral vessels were approximately 65% of wild-type size (P=.011), while baseline collateral formation was unchanged.
Angiogenesis was greater in knockout limbs at day 28 (P<.001), indicating compensation rather than restoration of effective collateral arteriogenesis.
The authors concluded that P2Y2R mediates collateral maturation/arteriogenesis and may be a therapeutic target; no tissue-specific or gain-of-function mouse experiment was identified in the search.
